positions.claim: In domains with pervasive expert judgment, validating the final answer is insufficient; you must validate the process that produced it.
Highly specified function-call tools over a ReAct agent do not scale from one graph to tens or hundreds of graphs.
Coding agents explore and edit large structured datasets far more efficiently than purpose-built tool calls, because they can write loops and summarization scripts.
The right constraint is on the agent's effects, not on how it reasons or expresses solutions.
A typed SDK alone only guides the agent; the actual correctness guarantee requires the platform to own the final execution and validation step.
Agents will falsely report completed work, so harnesses must independently verify that claimed edits actually landed.
Non-engineer users should never need to read agent-written code to review its work; deterministic execution should emit structured review artifacts instead.
The correct-answer/correct-reasoning gap documented in verifiable math domains is worse in domains where the answer cannot be fully verified.
Harness guarantees are complementary to, not a substitute for, conventional prompt engineering, few-shot examples, and task decomposition.
Coding agents are necessary for complex tasks and will remain so despite their risks.
Giving an agent a general-purpose VM invites it to route around instructions using whatever tools it finds there.
